wy.title: West Yorkshire Tai Chi · main-form video index
wy.author: Mark and Kate Popplewell / West Yorkshire Tai Chi
wy.note: 41 lesson links cover movements 1–140. The last lesson combines gathering and finishing. Names and movement ranges are factual catalogue metadata. Videos remain with their publisher; their descriptions are not a frame-by-frame visual audit.

angie.title: Angie Wood · 42-set course index
angie.author: Angie Wood
angie.note: Names corroborate the sequence structure. Public summaries supply brief later teaching descriptions, not a transcription of Chee Soo’s book. Set 9 is spelt ‘Stalk’ on this site; the video index and Gibbon tradition use ‘Stork’. Sets 41 and 42 are separate listings, without an exact numbered boundary.

gibbon.title: Howard Gibbon · The First Five Sets
gibbon.author: Howard Gibbon / East–West Publications
gibbon.note: 37-page PDF. Opening photographs: printed/PDF pages 24, 26, 28, 30 and 32. Text faces them on the preceding page. Copyright notice on page 3 permits electronic distribution without alteration or sale and prohibits printing. The local copy is byte-for-byte unchanged. Photographs show Gibbon’s teaching material, not Chee Soo in the 1970s.

book.title: Chee Soo · The Chinese Art of T’ai Chi Ch’uan
book.author: Chee Soo; current publisher Seahorse Books
book.note: Publisher describes photographs of all 140 movements and says its reprint retains the Aquarian edition’s text, photographs and pagination. ISBN 9780954524401. Full plates were not directly inspected in this research; no historical image-to-movement matches are asserted. Publisher pages were intermittently unavailable.
book.accessNote: Direct fetch returned HTTP 503 on 24 October 2026; description read through the indexed publisher page.

bibliography.title: Seahorse Books · Chee Soo bibliography and life story
bibliography.author: Seahorse Books
bibliography.note: Lists 1976 Gordon and Cremonesi ISBN 0860330370, 1984 Aquarian Press ISBN 0850303877, and 2003 Seahorse ISBN 9780954524401. Publisher testimony about early lineage is not independent corroboration. The pictured archer-like pose is explicitly captioned as the Tai Chi dance.
bibliography.accessNote: Direct fetch returned HTTP 503 on 24 October 2026; bibliography read through the indexed page.

interview.title: Chee Soo interviewed by John R. Jones, April 1992
interview.author: Chee Soo / John R. Jones; edited by Taoist Arts Organisation
interview.note: Page 2 states 140 movements and distinguishes the main form from Flying Hands. The lineage story is Chee Soo’s testimony, not independently verified ancestry. This edited reprint includes medical claims; those are not adopted by this archive.
interview.accessNote: The search reader supplied the two-page PDF text, but a direct fetch returned HTTP 404 on 24 October 2026.

swanson.title: Tony Swanson on Lee-style taijiquan
swanson.author: Tony Swanson interviewed by FFAEMC
swanson.note: Describes 42 sequences / 140 movements, with the first 15 sequences / 50 movements as the short portion. Discusses bodily coordination and the compact floor area. The French account is a later school’s explanation.
swanson.accessNote: Article text was available in the search index; direct access redirected to the federation homepage on 24 October 2026.

pearson.title: Carl Pearson · Questions about Lee history
pearson.author: Carl Pearson
pearson.note: Discusses the lack of corroborating documentation for Chan Lee and the uncertainties of origin stories. This is a practitioner’s assessment; it neither proves nor disproves a proposed genealogy.

archive-variant.title: Archived Taoist Arts Organisation · The Form
archive-variant.author: Taoist Arts Organisation; mirror of telecentres.com material
archive-variant.note: This page gives 142 movements / 41 sequences, unlike Chee Soo’s edited interview and later 140 / 42 descriptions. The count is recorded as unresolved, not silently normalised or used to renumber this catalogue.

lute.title: Keith Ewers · Play the Lute
lute.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
lute.note: Contrasts palm orientations and arm levels between versions, and names martial force relationships. Links to the author’s illustrated page; no image reuse licence identified.

weaving.title: Keith Ewers · Fair Lady Weaves the Shuttle
weaving.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
weaving.note: Describes the third named passage through weight transfer and reversing arm circles.

waist.title: Keith Ewers · Turning the waist and hips
waist.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
waist.note: Uses Repulse the Monkey and Crane as examples of his waist/hip distinction. Read as his teaching account, not a prescription for forced spinal rotation.

bump.title: Keith Ewers · The Bumping Method
bump.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
bump.note: Discusses an application within Crane and includes a later photograph of Ewers. Not evidence that every school teaches the same application.

tiger.title: Keith Ewers · Drive Tiger Away to the Mountain
tiger.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
tiger.note: Gives an advance, retreat and return interpretation and a partner application. A later school’s interpretation rather than a historical plate caption.

bird.title: Keith Ewers · Grasp the Bird’s Tail
bird.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
bird.note: Describes withdrawing to Cat stance and stepping right. The shared name does not establish identity with Yang Grasp Sparrow’s Tail.

pluck.title: Keith Ewers · The Plucking Method
pluck.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
pluck.note: Names Single Whip and Grasp the Bird’s Tail as examples; also acknowledges differing finger arrangements between his current method and his recollection of earlier teaching.

brush.title: Keith Ewers · Brush Knee and Side Step
brush.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
brush.note: Stresses simultaneous hand movement and waist-led sweeps; explicitly disputes other versions.

stork.title: Keith Ewers · The Stork Is Aroused
stork.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
stork.note: Describes four phases and their force relationships. A useful later account rather than proof of the historical book’s exact execution.

double.title: Keith Ewers · Double Whip variants
double.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
double.note: Recollects differences between earlier and later teaching, particularly upright versus downward-facing palms. The proposed chronology remains attributed testimony.

double-practice.title: Keith Ewers · Double Whip practice
double-practice.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
double-practice.note: Discusses force relationships and different ways of practising the passage separately. Those exercises are not substituted for the main form here.

cyclone.title: Keith Ewers · Edge of the Cyclone
cyclone.author: Keith Ewers / LFIAA
cyclone.note: Focuses on connected circular movement; does not supply a numbered reconstruction of the historical form.
